question: Your extraction agent reads scanned order forms and calls a customer lookup tool with the extracted customer name to link each order to an account. For one form, the tool returns three customer records with the same name in different cities. The extraction agent currently links the order to the record with the most recent activity, and audits show that some orders reach the wrong accounts. Which change best fixes this behavior?

options.text: Instruct the extraction agent to request an additional identifier, such as an account number or billing address, before it links the order to any record.
options.reason: The guide says that multiple matches require clarification by requesting additional identifiers rather than selecting a record by a heuristic.

options.text: Instruct the extraction agent to report a self-assessed confidence score for each candidate record and link the order automatically when the top score exceeds 0.9.
options.reason: The guide says that self-reported confidence scores are unreliable, and this choice still selects a record without requesting an additional identifier.

options.text: Instruct the extraction agent to choose the record whose city most closely matches the shipping address on the form, because location is the strongest available signal.
options.reason: This replaces one heuristic with another heuristic, and the guide says that multiple matches need additional identifiers instead of heuristic selection.

options.text: Keep the most-recent-activity rule but add an output field that lists the other matching record IDs so that downstream systems can review them later.
options.reason: The order is still linked by a heuristic, while the guide requires clarification with additional identifiers when there are multiple matches.
